'''John Michael David Coey''' (24 February 1945 – 6 October 2025), known as '''Michael Coey''', was a Northern Irish-born experimental physicist working in the fields of [[magnetism]] and [[spintronics]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=2025-10-08 |title=Professor Mike Coey |url=https://ambercentre.ie/professor-mike-coey/ |website=ambercentre.ie |publisher=Research Ireland Centre for Advanced Materials and BioEngineering Research |access-date=2025-10-09}}</ref> He was a professor at the [[Trinity College Dublin]] (TCD).<ref name="IOP News-2019">{{Cite news |date=3 April 2019 |title=Max Born Medal and Prize for 2019 goes to Professor Michael Coey |work=IOP News |url=https://www.iop.org/about/news/max-born-medal-and-prize-2019-goes-to-professor-michael-coey#gref}}</ref>

== Life and career ==

=== Education ===
Michael Coey completed a BA in Physics at [[Jesus College, Cambridge]] in 1966; he then travelled across Europe and Asia, teaching English and Physics in India.<ref name=NLM /> He completed his PhD from [[University of Manitoba]] (1971) for a thesis on "Mössbauer Effect of <sup>57</sup>Fe in Magnetic Oxides" with advisor Allan H. Morrish.<ref name="pnas">Lifland (2009)</ref>

He was at the physics department of [[Trinity College Dublin]] (TCD) from 1978. He obtained his ScD in 1987 and passed his [[Habilitation]] from the [[University of Grenoble]] in 1986, and an honorary doctorate in 1994. He served as [[Erasmus Smith's Professor of Natural and Experimental Philosophy]] at TCD from 2007 to 2012.<ref>[https://www.tcd.ie/Physics/research/groups/magnetism/group/coey/index.php Prof. Michael Coey] TCD: School of Physics</ref> After retirement, he was an [[:wikt:Emeritus|Emeritus]] professor at TCD.

=== Career ===
Coey was a Professor of Physics at TCD from 1987, and was appointed [[Erasmus Smith's Professor of Natural and Experimental Philosophy at Trinity College Dublin|Erasmus Smith's Professor of Natural and Experimental Philosophy]] (2007–2012), a chair that dates from 1724.<ref>[https://www.maths.tcd.ie/about/400Hist/7.php Erasmus Smith's professors of Mathematics] Mathematics at TCD 1592–1992</ref>

In 1994 Coey founded Magnetic Solutions and went on to be the cofounder of [[CRANN]] Ireland's Nanoscience Research institute (2002) and conceived Dublin's unique Science Gallery (2006).<ref name="pnas" /> 

His textbook ''Magnetism and Magnetic Materials''<ref>{{Cite book|title=Magnetism and magnetic materials|last=Coey|first=John M.D.|date=2009|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-81614-4|location=Cambridge|oclc=664016090}}</ref> has been well received.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-3-030-63210-6   |title= Handbook of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Springer |publisher= |access-date= September 22, 2025 |quote=}}</ref>     

He delivered a public lecture on the History of Magnetism in Paris in 2010.{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} He held positions at [[National University of Singapore|National University Singapore]] and the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids]] in Dresden.{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} He also worked with [[Beihang University]] in Beijing for five years.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0053-8452 |title= John Michael David Coey |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= ORCID |publisher= |access-date= September 22, 2025 |quote=}}</ref>     

He was part of numerous collaborations including: [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center|IBM Yorktown Heights]] (1979), Institute of Physics Peking (1980), [[McGill University]] (1982), [[University of Bordeaux]] (1984), CEN-Grenoble (1985), Johns Hopkins APL (1986), [[Universite de Paris IV]] (1992), [[University of California, San Diego]]  (1997), [[Florida State University]] (1998), University of Paris XI (1998), [[Leman University Geneva]] (2001/3), [[University of Strasbourg]] (2006).{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}}

Coey pioneered a co-operation project between academic and industrial laboratories in the Concerted European Action on Magnets (1985–95).<ref name=NLM />  Throughout his career he strongly identified himself with the European spirit and tradition of collaboration.{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}}

By 2009, he had published more than 600 articles and filed 25 patents.<ref name=NLM />  In late 2025, his [[H-index]] was 116.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=6z12KzAAAAAJ&hl=en |title= JMD Coey |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 27 May 2009 |website= Scholar Google |publisher= |access-date= September 22, 2025 |quote=}}</ref>  

=== Personal life and death ===
Coey was married to poet [[Wong May|Wong May Coey]] in 1973 and had two sons.<ref name="poetry.sg a850">{{cite web | title=Wong May / Bio | website=poetry.sg | url=http://www.poetry.sg/wong-may-bio | access-date=26 November 2023}}</ref><ref name="Springer International Publishing 2021 p. ">{{cite book | title=Handbook of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials | publisher=Springer International Publishing | publication-place=Cham | year=2021 | isbn=978-3-030-63208-3 | doi=10.1007/978-3-030-63210-6 | page= | editor-last1=Coey | editor-last2=Parkin | editor-first1=J. M. D. | editor-first2=Stuart S.P. }}</ref>

Coey died on 6 October 2025, at the age of 80.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Coey |url=https://rip.ie/death-notice/michael-coey-dublin-607622 |website=[[RIP.ie]] |date=2025-10-09 |access-date=2025-10-09 |language=en}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
 
Coey was a member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]] (1987),<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor John Michael David Coey |url=https://www.ria.ie/members/professor-john-michael-david-coey/ |website=www.ria.ie |publisher=[[Royal Irish Academy]] |access-date=2025-10-09}}</ref> a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (2003) and a Foreign Associate of the US [[National Academy of Sciences]] (2005).<ref name=NLM>{{cite web |url= https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2690015/  |title= Profile of John Michael David Coey |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 27 May 2009 |website= National Library of Medicine |publisher= |access-date= September 22, 2025 |quote=}}</ref>   He was also a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]], the [[Mineralogical Society of America]] and the [[American Physical Society]]. 

His numerous awards included a [[Fulbright Fellowship]], the [[Charles Chree Medal]] of the Institute of Physics (1997), the Gold Medal of the Royal Irish Academy (2005) the RDS INTEL Prize Lecture on [[Nanoscience]] (2012) in addition to being the recipient of the Gutenberg (2015) and [[Max Born Medal and Prize]] (2019) awards. He also won the [[Humboldt Prize]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview/1150880/prof-dr-john-michael-david-coey  |title= Profile: Prof. Dr. John Michael David Coey |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Humboldt Foundation |publisher= |access-date= September 22, 2025 |quote=}}</ref> He received the [[Max Born Medal and Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] in 2012.<ref name="IOP News-2019" /> 

He received an honorary doctorate from the [[Grenoble Institute of Technology|Institute National Polytechnique Grenoble]] (1994) and had been a Distinguished Lecturer, [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] Magnetics Study (2006) and the Albert Einstein Professor of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (2010). In 2023, he was awarded an honorary D.Sc. by Trinity College Dublin.<ref>{{cite web |date=2024-11-22 |title=Honorary Degrees 2023-2024 |url=https://www.tcd.ie/registrar/honorary-degrees/2023-24/index.php |website=Trinity College Dublin |publisher= |access-date=2025-10-09}}</ref>

In 2000, he was awarded funding from [[Science Foundation Ireland]], which went towards the creation of the [[CRANN|Centre for Research on Adaptive Nanostructures and Nanodevices]] at TCD.<ref name=NLM />
